reasoning: A hybrid strategy combines autonomous reasoning to identify candidate spurious features through cross-instance pattern recognition with external XAI tools to validate and quantify feature importance, ensuring both pattern detection and model-level attribution. This approach balances interpretability with rigorous attribution analysis, especially when ground truth labels are unknown and feature semantics are ambiguous.

autonomous_tasks.query: Which features are present in all three misclassified instances (541, 537, 128) and have similar values across them?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: List of shared features across all three instances with value ranges

autonomous_tasks.query: Why might high values in mean radius or mean area be spurious indicators of malignancy when ground truth is unknown?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: Hypothesis about spurious correlation between size-based features and malignancy prediction

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP identifies feature importance across instances with a game-theoretic guarantee, integrated gradients provide gradient-based attribution sensitive to input distribution, and sensitivity analysis isolates features whose removal causes large prediction shifts—collectively revealing shared spurious features despite missing ground truth. The intersection mode ensures shared importance among misclassified instances.
